(1) Apache Egypt Companies 'Environmental Impact Assessment: Oil & Gas Activities' (Firebird, Feb. 2004), hosted at miga.org (World Bank Group MIGA) -- pdftotext confirms verbatim on the Salam and Tarek gas-plant process pages: 'This crude oil line runs from Meliha to El Hamra terminal. It is owned and operated by Agiba Oil Company' (16-inch line, condensate/crude fed into it from both plants). NOTE: url_verifier content-check FAILs on 'Meleiha'/'El-Hamra' against this PDF -- this is the documented large-PDF extractor false-negative (verifier docstring), not evidence the content is absent; manual pdftotext confirms the exact text at multiple points. (2) EgyptOil&Gas 'The Western Desert: Egypt's Giant Petroleum Reservoir' (egyptoil-gas.com, 2020) states outright 'The Western Desert has four crude oil pipelines. Three pipelines transport crude oil from the production areas, specifically from Meleiha, Badr El Din, and Abu Gharadig concessions to El Hamra terminal ... then is shipped by the fourth pipeline, El Hamra-Sidi Kerir, to refineries in Alexandria' and gives a table: Meleiha-El Hamra | Meleiha Fields -> El Hamra | 167 km | 16 in | 90,000 (bpd). The other three rows of that same table match the roster EXACTLY: Badr El Din-El Hamra 128 km/12 in/60,000 = P3689; Abu Gharadig-El Hamra 140 km/12,16 in/60,000 = P3688; El Hamra-Sidi Kerir-Alexandria 90 km/16 in/200,000 = P3693 -- which cross-validates the table's reliability for this row too. GEM's LengthKnown (167.00 km) and Diameter (16.00 in) both match this table exactly; StartLocation 'Mleiha oilfield' / EndLocation 'El Hamra terminal' match both sources; Fuel=Oil and Status=operating are both consistent with 'crude oil pipeline' language in an infrastructure table published as current in 2020 and described as actively receiving flow in 2004. This is a real, correctly-classified crude-oil trunk pipeline -- not a phantom or misfiled NGL/gas line.

validity.researcher_notes: Checked against the orchestrator's watchlist question: is P0572 'Mleiha-El Hamra' (167 km, 16 in, 140,000 bpd, Mleiha oilfield) the same physical line as P5125 'Southwest Mleiha Pipeline' (130 km, 10 in, 7,000 bpd, Southwest Mleiha->Matruh)? The EgyptOil&Gas 2020 source is explicit that 'The Western Desert has four crude oil pipelines' and names exactly four: Meleiha-El Hamra, Badr El Din-El Hamra, Abu Gharadig-El Hamra, and El Hamra-Sidi Kerir-Alexandria -- matching P0572, P3689, P3688, P3693 one-for-one, with NO fifth 'Southwest Mleiha' line among the majors. Combined with the differing diameter (16 in vs 10 in), length (167 vs 130 km) and an order-of-magnitude capacity difference (140,000/90,000 vs 7,000 bpd), P5125 reads as a smaller satellite/gathering line off the separate Southwest Mleiha discovery (a named sub-field distinct from the main Meleiha field per the 2020 report's field history section), not a relabeling or segment double-count of P0572. Per the scope guidance's own heuristic (same name + same diameter/length = suspicious; different diameter = usually two real parallel/distinct lines), this pair reads as two real, separate pipelines.
